intro: While Murmur is open it serves an HTTP API, so other programs, devices on your local network, and agents can transcribe audio through it. API jobs share the same inference queue as the app, and their results also appear in the history on the left.

lan.label: Allow local network access
lan.hint: Other computers and phones on the same network can call it; turn this off on public networks

port.label: Port
port.invalid: Port must be an integer between 1024 and 65535

addresses.title: Server addresses
addresses.lanHint: Use this address on other devices
addresses.lanWarning: The local network API has no password, so any device on the same network can submit transcription jobs. Other devices can only upload files; they cannot read files on this Mac or browse history.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.health: Server status, loaded model, and its supported languages
endpoints.transcribe: Upload an audio/video file to transcribe; output as json / txt / srt / vtt / md
endpoints.job: Check the progress of an async job; includes the result when finished
endpoints.export: Export a transcript in the given format
endpoints.models: List models and their install status

examples.title: Examples
examples.uploadSrt: Upload a file and get SRT subtitles directly
examples.getJson: Get JSON (with segments and word-level timestamps)

skill.title: Agent Skill
skill.hint: Copy to your agent's skills folder (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/) and the agent will transcribe audio with Murmur
